title: Rooms Keys Browse — payload
description: TODO: what the request payload of rooms/keys/browse carries. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

roomId.description: The room to list. The recipient MUST already hold group state for it.

host.description: The host to list from, as a DID. Named by the caller for the same reason it is on `rooms/keys/read`: nothing maps a room to its host.

prefix.description: Restrict to keys with this prefix. Passed through to the host. **Setting it makes the listing non-comparable against the room's `recordCount`** — see `verification.count`.

sinceVersion.description: Return only records above this version. Passed through. Also makes the listing non-comparable against `recordCount`.

beforeVersion.description: Return only records whose current version is below this — an exclusive upper bound, passed through to the host's `rooms/records/list/0.8`. A surface paging a conversation backwards passes the lowest version it holds. Also makes the listing non-comparable against `recordCount`.

order.description: Passed through to the host. `oldestFirst` (the default when absent) or `newestFirst`, which reads the room's head first: with `maxPages`, the shape a member's surface uses to open a conversation at its newest messages.

limit.description: Page size to ask the host for. A cap on what a page holds, never a cap on the result: a recipient MUST follow the host's cursor to the end unless the caller asked it to stop with `maxPages`, or it stopped of its own accord, because a listing read to its end is the only one whose length means anything.

maxPages.description: The most host pages the recipient reads for this request. Absent, it reads to the end unless it stops of its own accord. A recipient that stops here with more records remaining answers `complete: false` and the host's continuation as `nextCursor`. Setting it makes the listing non-comparable against `recordCount` unless the end is reached within it.

cursor.description: A `nextCursor` from an earlier browse of the same room at the same host, with the same `prefix`, `sinceVersion`, `beforeVersion` and `order`. Passed through to the host as its listing's `cursor`; the host refuses one it did not issue or issued under another order or other bounds, and the recipient answers `hostRefused`. A listing resumed from a cursor does not start at the room's first record in its order, so it is never comparable against `recordCount`.

records.description: Metadata, never bodies — the same projection the host serves, passed through. A member who wants a body asks for one record, which is also the only shape a trace can be produced for.

complete.description: Whether the recipient followed the host's cursor to the end. `false` means a page bound was hit, and is what makes `verification.count` `notComparable` even on an unfiltered listing — a short listing and a truncated one are indistinguishable by length alone, which is exactly the confusion this member exists to prevent.

nextCursor.description: The host's continuation token, present exactly when `complete` is `false`: the recipient stopped — at `maxPages` or of its own accord — while the host still had records to list. Pass it back as `cursor`, with the same `prefix`, `sinceVersion`, `beforeVersion` and `order`, to continue. Absent when the listing reached its end.

verification.description: What the recipient checked and what it found. REQUIRED for the same reason it is on `rooms/keys/read`.

lastPrune.description: The room's latest record prune, passed through from the host's listing (`rooms/records/list` 0.3) exactly as served, whenever the room's records have been pruned. A caller keeping its own copy of the room synchronised below `lastPrune.version` rebuilds it from a browse with no `sinceVersion`, as `rooms/records/list` 0.3 *After a prune* requires.
